newsitem.title: USA: Racism panel should drop liberal ideas - Gingrich.
newsitem.headline: Racism panel should drop liberal ideas - Gingrich.

text.p: House Speaker Newt Gingrich said Friday that the panel President Clinton named this week to help fight racism will make progress only if it abandons "tired old big government liberalism."

In a news briefing, the Georgia Republican also said he expected this Congress would pass a bill to eliminate racial quotas, but said he wanted that in a "larger framework" of tax cuts to spur small businesses, improved inner-city education, and more inducements to get people off of welfare.

"I will move that bill in the context of other actions designed to dramatically improve the opportunities for people who were born into Indian reservations or inner cities, people who are black or Hispanic," Gingrich said.
Gingrich said he felt the panel Clinton named this week as part an initiative to combat racism will be helpful "because it begins a process of a real dialogue."
But he said he was concerned the panel would push racial quotas and setasides that would not produce real solutions.

"My fear is that the composition of this commission, which is very, very traditional in its assumptions about government, and the direction of the president's effort to maintain quotas and setasides will...divert us and make it harder to solve problems," Gingrich said.
"Unless the commission has a dramatically different agenda and a different approach, the same tired old big government liberalism will be like commissions we've had for 30 years," he said.
